sources.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis, 8 June 2017 manuscript
sources.locator: Theorem 2.71 pp.89–91; Theorem 2.73 p.93 (PDF pp.96–98,100, zero-based)

contents.name: Theorem 2.71(i): reflexivity of the dual
contents.support: Algebraic canonical-map argument and Hahn–Banach annihilator argument; real source translated to scalar-linear complex duals.

contents.name: Theorem 2.71(ii): closed subspaces
contents.support: Pull back a bidual functional along dual restriction and annihilate the orthogonal subspace.

contents.name: Theorem 2.71(ii): quotient spaces
contents.support: Extend from the quotient annihilator to X* and represent by a vector; no closed-ball-surjectivity assumption.

contents.name: Theorem 2.73(i): separable dual implies separable primal
contents.support: Countable almost-norming vectors and annihilator density; handle the zero space explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 2.73(ii): reflexive separable dual
contents.support: Apply part (i) to X* and identify the canonical bidual.

sources.title: Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations
sources.locator: Proposition 3.20 p.70; Theorem 3.26 and Corollary 3.27 pp.73–74; definition and Theorem 3.31 pp.76–78

contents.name: Proposition 3.20: closed reflexive subspaces
contents.support: Hahn–Banach identifies the intrinsic and relative weak topologies; closed unit subball is weakly compact.

contents.name: Theorem 3.26
contents.support: Norm-dense functionals, chosen almost-norming vectors, and annihilator separation.

contents.name: Corollary 3.27
contents.support: The double dual is separable under reflexivity.

contents.name: Section 3.7: uniformly convex space
contents.support: Unit-ball midpoint condition; strict versus weak inequalities are translated using epsilon/2.

contents.name: Theorem 3.31: Milman–Pettis
contents.support: Goldstine and a small almost-norming weak-star slice force norm approximation of any bidual unit vector. The source is real; complex adaptation uses real parts.

contents.name: Theorem A.4(i)–(vii): unconditional convergence equivalences
contents.support: Permutation, common sum, unordered net, finite-tail, uniform scalar-tail, bounded-multiplier, and subseries conditions. Complex scalar estimate uses four sign groups. Replace the Cauchy-net completeness appeal by an explicit ordinary partial-sum limit.

contents.name: A.2 introductory unconditional series terminology
contents.support: Convergence under every permutation does not assume common sums until A.4 proves that property.
